PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108") or SHA1 in~ ("ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108") or MD5 in~ ("ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108") or SHA1 in~ ("ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108") or MD5 in~ ("ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 — archive tool writes payload to user Startup folder AIInstallation High
Detects the smoking-gun signature of CVE-2025-8088 NTFS ADS path traversal: WinRAR/Rar/UnRAR/7zG writing files into %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup — the exact persistence drop chain used by SHADOW-EARTH-066 (GIFTEDCROOK) and Earth Dahu (GammaPhish/GammaLoad) campaigns against Ukrainian organisations. Rationale: Article explicitly states the CVE-2025-8088 exploit chain drops an LNK 'placed in the Startup folder so that it's automatically executed every time a user logs in' — combining archive-tool parent with Startup-folder destination + autostart extension is article-specific and behaviourally near-zero-FP. Cross-checked against Trend Micro disclosure and ESET's earlier RomCom write-up of the same CVE. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-8088 • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/romcom-exploits-winrar-zero-day-cve-2025-8088/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0047/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1574.005 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT-deployed software bundles where WinRAR/7-Zip is used in scripted installers that legitimately drop launcher shortcuts into the Startup folder
  • User extracts a legitimate portable app archive and manually pins an LNK into Startup (rare but seen on dev/power-user workstations)
  • Backup-restore operations where an old user profile is recovered with Startup-folder content via WinRAR
  • Software-deployment tools (PDQ Deploy, SCCM staging) chain-calling WinRAR/UnRAR to expand a vendor MSI bundle
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PDQDeploy","sccm","sccmclient","InstallShield","setup.exe") and InitiatingProcessAccountName endswith "$")
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the dropped artefact (LNK/EXE/DLL), SHA256 it, and check VT + the article's known-bad hashes; inspect the parent RAR file in DownloadedFiles / mail attachments. 2) Contain — isolate the host via MDE Live Response, kill any running powershell/cmd/mshta children spawned in the next 5 minutes, and quarantine the dropped Startup artefact. 3) Hunt — sweep the org for the parent RAR hash, any sibling NTFS:$DATA ADS writes by the same WinRAR process tree, and pivot on the user mailbox for the inbound phishing message that delivered the archive (last 14 days).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("WinRAR.exe","Rar.exe","UnRAR.exe","7zG.exe","Bandizip.exe")
| where FolderPath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup"
| where FileName endswith ".lnk" or FileName endswith ".exe" or FileName endswith ".dll" or FileName endswith ".bat" or FileName endswith ".vbs" or FileName endswith ".hta" or FileName endswith ".cmd" or FileName endswith ".ps1"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("winrar.exe","rar.exe","unrar.exe","7zg.exe","bandizip.exe")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup"
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("lnk","exe","dll","bat","vbs","hta","cmd","ps1")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 ADS Path Traversal — Archive Tool Writes to Startup Folder
id: 9b3f8e2a-1f5d-4c1a-9b3e-5e7f8c2d4a1b
description: Detects archive extraction utilities writing autostart payloads to the user Startup folder, the smoking-gun signature of CVE-2025-8088 NTFS ADS path traversal abuse used by SHADOW-EARTH-066 and Earth Dahu against Ukrainian targets.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/winrar-flaw-exploited-by-russia-aligned.html
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.t1547.001
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  archive_tool:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\WinRAR.exe'
      - '\Rar.exe'
      - '\UnRAR.exe'
      - '\7zG.exe'
      - '\Bandizip.exe'
  startup_path:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\'
  autostart_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.lnk'
      - '.exe'
      - '.dll'
      - '.bat'
      - '.vbs'
      - '.hta'
      - '.cmd'
      - '.ps1'
  condition: archive_tool and startup_path and autostart_ext
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\WinRAR.exe OR *\winrar.exe OR *\Rar.exe OR *\rar.exe OR *\UnRAR.exe OR *\unrar.exe OR *\7zG.exe OR *\Bandizip.exe) @TargetFilename:(*"\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\"* OR *"\\start menu\\programs\\startup\\"*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/(WinRAR|Rar|UnRAR|7zG|Bandizip)\.exe$/i
| TargetFileName=/\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\.*\.(lnk|exe|dll|bat|vbs|hta|cmd|ps1)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("WinRAR.exe","Rar.exe","UnRAR.exe","7zG.exe","Bandizip.exe") AND Filesystem.file_path="*\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\*" AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.lnk" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.exe" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.dll" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.vbs" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.bat" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.hta" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.cmd" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.ps1") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Startup LNK spawns cmd.exe → PowerShell in-memory DLL loader (GIFTEDCROOK chain) AIInstallation High
Catches the GIFTEDCROOK post-extraction loader chain: explorer.exe auto-runs a Startup LNK that invokes cmd.exe which spawns powershell.exe carrying in-memory reflective-load primitives to launch result.dll. Article calls out cmd→PowerShell→reflective-load as the exact sequence. Rationale: Article describes the chain verbatim: 'LNK in Startup folder ... spawns a PowerShell loader via cmd.exe, which then uses in-memory DLL loading to ultimately launch ... result.dll.' Triple-anchor (Startup-LNK parent + cmd→PS + reflective-load tokens) is highly article-specific and rare in benign traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1620/ • https://www.cert.gov.ua/article/giftedcrook
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1620 T1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate sysadmin login script that uses cmd.exe → powershell.exe -EncodedCommand from an admin's pinned Startup shortcut
  • Citrix/RDS broker scripts triggered from per-user logon LNKs (some EHRs/VDI gold images still ship these)
  • Vendor monitoring/inventory tools that use cmd→PS reflective load (LANDesk, older Tanium build-out scripts)
  • Developer-machine PowerShell profile that imports modules via Reflection.Assembly from a Startup shim
Suppression filter
| where not (ActorUsername has_any ("admin","svc-") and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Import-Module","-File \\\\","\\Scripts\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — capture the powershell.exe command line + decode any base64; if it references result.dll or in-memory load, treat as confirmed GIFTEDCROOK loader and pull the Startup LNK + its $DATA streams. 2) Contain — isolate host, kill the powershell.exe tree, quarantine the LNK target and any DLLs written by the PS session in the prior 60 seconds. 3) Hunt — query DeviceNetworkEvents from the powershell.exe ProcessId for callbacks to the article's IPs/domains; sweep all hosts for the same LNK target hash and same parent RAR.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "cmd.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "explorer.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Startup\", @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup", ".lnk")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("FromBase64String","IEX","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString","Reflection.Assembly","[Reflection.Assembly]","::Load(","-nop","-w hidden","-windowstyle hidden","-enc","result.dll")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has "cmd.exe"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Startup\", @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup", ".lnk")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("FromBase64String","IEX","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString","Reflection.Assembly","::Load(","-nop","hidden","-enc","result.dll")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE) @ParentCommandLine:(*"\\Startup\\"* OR *"\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup"* OR *.lnk*) @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:(*FromBase64String* OR *Reflection.Assembly* OR *::Load(* OR *IEX* OR *Invoke-Expression* OR *-nop* OR *hidden* OR *-enc* OR *result.dll*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/cmd\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| ParentCommandLine=/(\\Startup\\|\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup|\.lnk)/i
| regex("(FromBase64String|Reflection\\.Assembly|::Load\\(|IEX|Invoke-Expression|-nop|hidden|-enc|result\\.dll)", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

GIFTEDCROOK browser credential and cookie theft — non-browser process reads Chromium/Firefox stores AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects GIFTEDCROOK's credential-collection stage: a process that is NOT the browser itself opens the Login Data, Cookies, Web Data or Firefox key4.db/logins.json/cookies.sqlite files inside the user's browser profile directories. Article names Chrome, Edge, Opera and Firefox as the targets. Rationale: Article enumerates exact targets: 'passwords and cookies from Chromium-based browsers (Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera) and Mozilla Firefox.' File-access pattern from non-browser process is the highest-signal credential-theft pivot available without YARA. Matches GIFTEDCROOK behavior in Trend Micro and CERT-UA reports. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/giftedcrook • https://blog.sekoia.io/gamaredon-toolset/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Credential-manager browser plugins backed by a helper EXE (1Password Helper, Bitwarden-cli)
  • Endpoint backup agents (Code42/CrashPlan, Druva) that snapshot the entire user profile including the browser data directory
  • DLP agents (Forcepoint, Netskope) that scan profile contents on first sync
  • User-account migration tools (USMT, Microsoft Edge Profile Importer, Chrome migration helper) during machine provisioning
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("1Password.exe","1PasswordHelper.exe","Bitwarden.exe","keeperpasswordmanager.exe","code42service.exe","crashplanservice.exe","druvainsync.exe","nsdiag.exe","fcdblog.exe","USMT.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — confirm the reading process is not on the allow-list; SHA256 the binary, check parent process tree back to explorer.exe/cmd.exe/PowerShell to determine entry vector. 2) Contain — isolate host, force-reset all stored credentials and active SSO sessions for the affected user (Entra revoke + browser-side sign-out), rotate any saved API keys, kill the offending process. 3) Hunt — pivot on InitiatingProcessSHA256 across the fleet; check DeviceNetworkEvents from the same ProcessId for exfil to article IOCs; review EmailEvents for the inbound RAR.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Opera Software\Opera Stable\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\", @"\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\User Data\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","Web Data","key4.db","logins.json","cookies.sqlite","places.sqlite")
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","opera.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","explorer.exe","MsMpEng.exe","SearchIndexer.exe","backgroundTaskHost.exe"))
| where not (InitiatingProcessAccountName endswith "$")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Opera Software\Opera Stable\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\", @"\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\User Data\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","Web Data","key4.db","logins.json","cookies.sqlite","places.sqlite")
| where not(ActingProcessName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","opera.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","explorer.exe","MsMpEng.exe","SearchIndexer.exe","backgroundTaskHost.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GIFTEDCROOK / Gamaredon C2 callback to article IOCs (IPs + workers.dev / trycloudflare / .ru domains) AICommand & Control Medium
Network-level pivot on the article's published infrastructure: three IPs and seven domains spanning Cloudflare Workers, trycloudflare quick tunnels and Russia-tied vanity domains used by SHADOW-EARTH-066 and Earth Dahu after pivoting away from Telegram as their exfil channel. Rationale: All ten IOCs are taken directly from the article's provided IOC bundle (3 IPs, 7 domains) and triangulate two distinct campaigns sharing the CVE. The workers.dev + trycloudflare-quick-tunnel + .ru-vanity-domain combination is the article-specific tradecraft signature post-Telegram-blocking pivot. Triple-pivot (DNS, network, proxy) maximises catch rate. Cross-checked against: • https://otx.alienvault.com/indicator/domain/dayobtvoyu.ru • https://www.virustotal.com/gui/ip-address/172.86.76.132 • https://blog.sekoia.io/gamaredon-toolset/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate dev/test traffic to other tenants on the workers.dev or trycloudflare.com shared CDN — possible but the specific subdomains are unique
  • Sandbox/research VM in the same network deliberately detonating GIFTEDCROOK samples
  • Threat-intel feed enrichment agent that performs active checks against the same IOCs
  • Security researcher browsing the article and clicking links to defanged-but-still-resolvable IOCs
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("CuckooMon.exe","vmtoolsd.exe","sandbox-agent.exe") or DeviceName has_any ("SANDBOX-","DETONATE-","MALLAB-"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — identify the InitiatingProcessFileName that made the call; if it's powershell/wscript/mshta/cmd/rundll32, treat as confirmed C2. 2) Contain — block the IPs at the firewall/secure-web-gateway, sinkhole the domains in internal DNS, isolate any host that connected in the last 30 days. 3) Hunt — for every host that touched any IOC pull the parent RAR file, LNK Startup artefact, and any FileWritten events under the user's AppData in the 24h before contact; check EmailEvents for the inbound message that delivered the archive.
let bad_domains = dynamic(["snterval.selltosell.ru","dayobtvoyu.ru","sweet.csxvl00328.workers.dev","csxvl00328.workers.dev","e097.yggjf81487.workers.dev","vids-road-christina-guards.trycloudflare.com","insight-sweet-drainage-appreciated.trycloudflare.com"]);
let bad_ips = dynamic(["172.86.76.132","144.172.88.24","172.86.72.243"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (bad_domains) or RemoteIP in (bad_ips)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let bad_domains = dynamic(["snterval.selltosell.ru","dayobtvoyu.ru","sweet.csxvl00328.workers.dev","csxvl00328.workers.dev","e097.yggjf81487.workers.dev","vids-road-christina-guards.trycloudflare.com","insight-sweet-drainage-appreciated.trycloudflare.com"]);
let bad_ips = dynamic(["172.86.76.132","144.172.88.24","172.86.72.243"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has_any (bad_domains) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, IndicatorType="DNS"),
    (ImNetworkSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DstIpAddr in (bad_ips) or DstHostname has_any (bad_domains) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, IndicatorType="Network"),
    (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DestinationIP in (bad_ips) or RequestURL has_any (bad_domains) or DestinationHostName has_any (bad_domains) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=DeviceName, SrcIpAddr=SourceIP, DstIpAddr=DestinationIP, DstHostname=DestinationHostName, URL=RequestURL, IndicatorType="Proxy")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Earth Dahu / Gamaredon HTA-to-VBScript chain (mshta.exe spawning wscript/cscript) AIDelivery High
Detects Earth Dahu's documented HTA-to-VBScript delivery chain: mshta.exe loading GammaPhish HTA, then spawning wscript.exe/cscript.exe to execute GammaLoad VBScript downloaders that pull GammaSteel. Article confirms this chain has been active since September 2025 and through at least April 2026. Rationale: Article quotes Trend Micro: 'Earth Dahu used the vulnerability with an HTA-to-VBScript infection chain that delivered espionage modules' — mshta.exe → wscript.exe parent-child with a remote/.hta argument is the canonical GammaPhish→GammaLoad pivot. Cross-checked with Sekoia's recent Gamaredon write-up and MITRE G0047. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/gamaredon-toolset/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0047/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/005/
ATT&CKT1218.005 T1059.005 T1105 T1568.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy line-of-business application that ships .hta installers (rare but seen in healthcare and Ukrainian government estates)
  • Sysadmin running diagnostic .hta scripts from Microsoft KB downloads
  • Vendor support tools (Dell SupportAssist older builds, some HP printer setup utilities) launched via mshta.exe
  • Internal IT job that wraps a vbscript downloader for software inventory
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("HELPDESK-","SCCM-") and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\\\corp.local\\","\\\\fileserver\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — extract the .hta URL/path from ParentCommandLine, fetch it in a sandbox, hash the dropped VBScript and compare against the article's published hashes (GammaLoad/GammaSteel families). 2) Contain — isolate the host, kill the mshta/wscript tree, block the .hta URL at the proxy, sinkhole any Dead-Drop-Resolver-style domain returned in the GammaLoad fetch chain. 3) Hunt — sweep DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound calls from wscript/cscript to non-Microsoft hosts in the last 30 days; pull EmailEvents and DeviceFileEvents from WinRAR for the inbound RAR that triggered the chain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "mshta.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (".hta","http://","https://","javascript:","vbscript:")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any (".vbs",".vbe",".js",".jse","GetObject(","WScript.Shell","MSXML2.XMLHTTP","WinHttp.WinHttpRequest")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildImage = FolderPath, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has "mshta.exe"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (".hta","http://","https://","javascript:","vbscript:")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (".vbs",".vbe",".js",".jse","GetObject(","WScript.Shell","MSXML2.XMLHTTP","WinHttp.WinHttpRequest")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Earth Dahu (Gamaredon) HTA-to-VBScript Infection Chain via mshta.exe

description: Detects the GammaPhish HTA → GammaLoad VBScript chain — mshta.exe loading a remote .hta and spawning wscript/cscript or PowerShell, as documented by Trend Micro and Sekoia for the Earth Dahu / Gamaredon WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 campaign.
references:

logsource:

detection:

    ParentImage|endswith: '\mshta.exe'
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - '.hta'
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - 'javascript:'
      - 'vbscript:'

    Image|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
  condition: parent_mshta and child_scripthost
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\mshta.exe OR *\MSHTA.EXE) @ParentCommandLine:(*.hta* OR *http\://* OR *https\://* OR *javascript\:* OR *vbscript\:*) @Image:(*\wscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe OR *\WSCRIPT.EXE OR *\cscript.exe OR *\CScript.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/mshta\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/(wscript|cscript|powershell|pwsh|cmd)\.exe$/i
| regex("(\.hta|https?://|javascript:|vbscript:)", field=ParentCommandLine, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentCommandLine, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="mshta.exe" AND Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_hash Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(parent_process,"(?i)\.(hta|html?)|https?://|javascript:|vbscript:")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="mshta.exe" AND Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_hash Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(parent_process,"(?i)\.(hta|html?)|https?://|javascript:|vbscript:")
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent

AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

union

        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — cross-operator admin API key mint via POST /api/v1/operators/{id}/api-keys AIExploitation High
Hunts the exact endpoint abused in exploit chain A — handleCreateOperatorAPIKey lacks any admin/ownership check pre-v0.3.4, so any successful POST to /api/v1/operators/{id}/api-keys by a non-admin actor mints a fresh bearer for an arbitrary operator (including admins). On an unpatched server this single request is privilege escalation. Rationale: Endpoint path /api/v1/operators/{id}/api-keys and the handleCreateOperatorAPIKey function at internal/api/operators.go:118 are quoted verbatim from the GHSA — exploit chain A delivers an admin bearer in one curl with no ownership check pre-v0.3.4. Successful POST on this exact path is the signal. No external corroboration available — CVE freshly minted (2026-47724) and GHSA is the authoritative source.
ATT&CKT1068 T1078.003 T1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin provisioning API keys for a newly created operator via the admin UI
  • Automated key rotation cron job owned by the ops team hitting this endpoint on a schedule
  • IaC/Terraform provider running operator-bootstrap during deployment
  • First-time setup script that seeds the initial admin operator and its API keys
  • Internal API health check or integration test that creates and immediately deletes a key
Suppression filter
// Sentinel example — suppress known admin sources and automation user-agents
| where cIP !in ("10.10.0.5", "10.10.0.6")  // ops bastion IPs
| where csUserAgent !startswith "terraform-provider-nebula/"
| where csUserAgent !contains "nebula-keyrotate-cron"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the bearer token's owning operator_id from the nebula-mesh app audit log for this request; if actor operator_id != target operator_id in the URL path, or actor is non-admin and target is an admin operator, treat as confirmed exploit. Capture the returned API key ID from the response body for forensics. 2) Contain: immediately revoke the newly minted bearer via DB-level UPDATE on operator_api_keys (do not use the API — attacker may still hold admin); rotate the source operator's key; force-upgrade the server to v0.3.4+. 3) Hunt: replay the last 30 days of /api/v1/operators/*/api-keys POSTs from the same source IP and bearer; pivot into /api/v1/hosts/*/reenroll, /api/v1/enroll, and /api/v1/networks/*/firewall calls within the same session window to scope blast radius.
// Primary: W3CIISLog when nebula-mesh is fronted by IIS/Azure App Gateway. Adapt cs* fields for AppServiceHTTPLogs or CommonSecurityLog (RequestURL/RequestMethod) as needed.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/operators/[^/]+/api-keys/?$"
| where scStatus in (200, 201)
| extend TargetOperatorId = extract(@"/api/v1/operators/([^/]+)/api-keys", 1, csUriStem)
| extend CVE = "CVE-2026-47724"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP=cIP, AuthUser=csUserName, csMethod, csUriStem, TargetOperatorId, scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent, CVE
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detects exploit chain B: a single source POSTs to /api/v1/hosts/{id}/reenroll (mints a single-use enrollment token for an arbitrary host with no ownership check) then immediately POSTs to /api/v1/enroll with attacker-controlled X25519/Ed25519 keys, overwriting signing_pub_pem and the cert. Same-source temporal correlation within ~60s on these two specific paths is the textbook exploitation signature. Rationale: Both endpoints (/api/v1/hosts/{id}/reenroll and /api/v1/enroll) and the temporal chain are explicitly walked in the article (internal/api/hosts.go:321,330 → mintEnrollmentTokenForHost, then enroll.go:175 overwrites signing_pub_pem). The 60-second window is generous — exploit code typically chains these in <5s. Sigma skipped because this is multi-event temporal correlation that single-event Sigma can't express.
ATT&CKT1098.001 T1212 T1552.004 T1550.001
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate operator-initiated identity rotation for a host whose key was suspected compromised
  • Automated post-incident reenrollment workflow rotating multiple hosts in sequence
  • Lab/staging environment provisioning script that reenrolls test hosts at deploy time
  • Agent recovery flow when a host's local key store is corrupted and ops triggers reenroll
  • Bulk migration tooling moving hosts between CAs (legitimately authorised admin action)
Suppression filter
// Sentinel — exclude known ops-bastion IPs and the legit reenrollment automation
| where cIP !in ("10.10.0.5", "10.10.0.6")
| where ReenrollAgent !startswith "nebula-rotate-cli/"
Response runbook
1) Triage: from the nebula-mesh DB, compare the bearer token's owning operator_id (actor) to the CAID of the host referenced in /hosts/{victim_host_id}/reenroll — if actor's operator does not own the host's CA, this is the exploit. Pull the signing_pub_pem and cert before/after rows from the hosts audit table. 2) Contain: invalidate the new cert on the affected host(s), force a fresh CA-signed reenroll from an admin operator, suspend the source bearer token, and force-upgrade to v0.3.4+. Watch for incoming 'bad_signature' poll failures from the legitimate agent — that confirms the identity was overwritten. 3) Hunt: for the same source IP and bearer, list every /hosts/*/reenroll and /enroll call across the lookback window to enumerate every host whose identity may have been seized; also pivot into /networks/*/firewall and /hosts/*/mobile-bundle activity from the same session.
let Lookback = 7d;
let WindowSec = 60;
let Reenroll = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where csMethod == "POST"
    | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/hosts/[^/]+/reenroll/?$"
    | where scStatus in (200, 201)
    | extend VictimHostId = extract(@"/api/v1/hosts/([^/]+)/reenroll", 1, csUriStem)
    | project ReenrollTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUserName, VictimHostId, ReenrollAgent = csUserAgent;
let Enroll = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where csMethod == "POST"
    | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/enroll/?$"
    | where scStatus in (200, 201)
    | project EnrollTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, EnrollAgent = csUserAgent;
Reenroll
| join kind=inner Enroll on cIP, Computer
| where EnrollTime between (ReenrollTime .. ReenrollTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', EnrollTime, ReenrollTime)
| extend CVE = "CVE-2026-47724"
| project ReenrollTime, EnrollTime, DelaySec, Computer, cIP, csUserName, VictimHostId, ReenrollAgent, EnrollAgent, CVE
| order by ReenrollTime desc

APPLICATION

nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — operator roster + API key metadata enumeration burst AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts the discovery phase of exploit chain A — a single source/bearer fanning out across GET /api/v1/operators and GET /api/v1/operators/{id}/api-keys (handleListOperators and handleListOperatorAPIKeys both lack admin gates per the GHSA) to identify admin operators and their key IDs before minting the privileged bearer. Rationale: Article enumerates the five operator-management handlers missing admin gates (operators.go:66 list, :79 disable, :94 enable, :157 revoke, :173 list-keys). Combining GET /api/v1/operators with multiple GET /api/v1/operators/{id}/api-keys in a short window is the natural recon shape before exploit A. Sigma skipped — threshold-based aggregation isn't expressible in single-event Sigma.
ATT&CKT1087 T1526 T1069.003
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Admin opening the operator-management dashboard, which fans out one list + per-operator key calls
  • Periodic operator inventory script run by ops to backup key metadata
  • SOC auditor performing a weekly access review across all operators
  • Monitoring/observability tooling polling these endpoints for an operator-health dashboard
  • Onboarding script for a new ops engineer exploring the API surface
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !startswith "nebula-admin-ui/"
| where csUserAgent !contains "nebula-audit-export"
Response runbook
1) Triage: in the nebula-mesh app audit log identify the bearer behind these GETs; if the actor's operator_id is non-admin AND the listed operator IDs include any admin operator, escalate. Inspect the response bodies (in the audit log) to confirm key metadata was returned. 2) Contain: if confirmed recon, rotate the suspect operator's bearer token immediately and tighten WAF/API-gateway rules to require admin auth on /api/v1/operators* before the v0.3.4 upgrade lands. 3) Hunt: from the same actor and source IP, pivot forward in time to any POST /api/v1/operators/*/api-keys (UC1), POST /api/v1/hosts/*/reenroll (UC2), or PUT /api/v1/networks/*/firewall (UC4) — recon almost always immediately precedes one of these.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod == "GET"
| where scStatus == 200
| where csUriStem == "/api/v1/operators" or csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/operators/[^/]+/api-keys/?$"
| summarize DistinctPaths = dcount(csUriStem),
            RequestCount = count(),
            SamplePaths = make_set(csUriStem, 20),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
          by cIP, csUserName, csUserAgent, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 3 or RequestCount >= 8
| extend CVE = "CVE-2026-47724"
| order by FirstSeen desc

nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — cross-tenant firewall mutation via PUT /api/v1/networks/{id}/firewall AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects state-changing writes to nebula-mesh firewall configuration on the /api/v1/networks/{id}/firewall endpoint, which trusts bearer auth alone pre-v0.3.4 per exploit chain C. An attacker with cross-tenant API access can open or remove firewall rules in any network in the deployment. Rationale: Article calls out /api/v1/networks/{id}/firewall (get, PUT) as part of exploit chain C and the CVSS rationale flags 'Mass cross-tenant CRUD including firewall-rule mutation' as a primary impact. Writes (PUT/POST) are the high-fidelity slice; reads would be too noisy.
ATT&CKT1562.007 T1565.001 T1098
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Operator updating firewall rules in a network they own via the admin UI
  • IaC/Terraform pipeline rolling out a routine network policy change
  • Scheduled rule reconciliation script flattening drift back to declared state
  • Incident-response playbook tightening rules in response to an unrelated alert
  • Migration tooling copying rules from a staging network to production
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !startswith "terraform-provider-nebula/"
| where csUserAgent !contains "nebula-policy-recon"
Response runbook
1) Triage: query the nebula-mesh app audit log for the actor's operator_id and the network's CAID — if actor's operator does not own the network's CA, treat as exploit chain C. Diff the firewall_rules table at request_time-1s vs request_time+1s to enumerate the exact rule changes. 2) Contain: revert the firewall_rules table from the audit log's pre-change snapshot, then suspend the source bearer and force-upgrade to v0.3.4+. If overly permissive rules were inserted (e.g. allow-any), block at the upstream network layer immediately. 3) Hunt: from the same actor and IP, pivot to GET /api/v1/networks/* for reconnaissance preceding the write, and to /hosts/*/reenroll (UC2) and /operators/*/api-keys (UC1) for the rest of the kill chain.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod in ("PUT", "POST")
| where csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/networks/[^/]+/firewall/?$"
| where scStatus in (200, 201, 204)
| extend NetworkId = extract(@"/api/v1/networks/([^/]+)/firewall", 1, csUriStem)
| extend CVE = "CVE-2026-47724"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP=cIP, AuthUser=csUserName, csMethod, csUriStem, NetworkId, scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent, CVE
| order by TimeGenerated desc

nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — operator sabotage (disable/enable/key revocation) by non-admin actor AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the impact phase of CVE-2026-47724 — handleDisableOperator (line 79), handleEnableOperator (line 94), and handleRevokeOperatorAPIKey (line 157) all lack admin gates per the GHSA. An exploited bearer can disable peer operators, re-enable disabled ones, or revoke any operator's API keys to lock legitimate admins out. Rationale: Article's 'Affected operator-management handlers' section explicitly lists each of these three handlers and their line numbers as missing admin gates. Disable/enable/revoke against a non-self target operator from a non-admin actor is unambiguous exploitation. Falcon, Defender, and CloudWatch all left empty: these are HTTP API calls to a custom Go server, not endpoint/AWS telemetry — only web-tier logs see them.
ATT&CKT1531 T1098 T1496
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Admin legitimately disabling an operator as part of offboarding a contractor
  • Admin re-enabling an operator after a paused review
  • Scheduled credential cleanup script revoking expired API keys
  • Break-glass rotation of an operator's keys after a perceived compromise
  • Bulk migration script consolidating operator accounts pre-v0.3.4 upgrade
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !startswith "nebula-offboard/"
| where csUserAgent !contains "nebula-keyrotate-cron"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the actor bearer's operator_id and admin flag from the nebula-mesh audit log — if actor is non-admin OR actor's operator_id != target operator_id, treat as confirmed sabotage. List every disabled operator and every revoked api_keys row touched by this actor in the lookback. 2) Contain: re-enable the affected peer operators directly via DB (bypass the API), regenerate revoked keys out-of-band, suspend the offending bearer, and force-upgrade to v0.3.4+ before re-opening the API. Notify affected operators via an out-of-band channel — they may be locked out of the API and need to be told. 3) Hunt: correlate forward into operator inventory (UC3), API key minting (UC1), and host reenroll chain (UC2) from the same actor — sabotage is usually the final stage; the recon and priv-esc happened earlier.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where scStatus in (200, 201, 204)
| where (csMethod == "POST" and (csUriStem endswith "/disable" or csUriStem endswith "/enable") and csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/operators/[^/]+/(disable|enable)/?$")
     or (csMethod == "DELETE" and csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/operators/[^/]+/api-keys/[^/]+/?$")
| extend TargetOperatorId = extract(@"/api/v1/operators/([^/]+)/", 1, csUriStem)
| extend Action = case(
    csUriStem endswith "/disable", "operator_disable",
    csUriStem endswith "/enable",  "operator_enable",
    csUriStem contains "/api-keys/", "api_key_revoke",
    "other")
| extend CVE = "CVE-2026-47724"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP=cIP, AuthUser=csUserName, csMethod, Action, TargetOperatorId, csUriStem, scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent, CVE
| order by TimeGenerated desc

osascript invoked with AppleScript breakout pattern (mismatched tell blocks + do shell script) AIExploitation High
Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-47252 in Anyquery: a SQL-controlled URL is interpolated unescaped into an AppleScript template and reaches `osascript -e`. The injected payload closes the original `tell application` block early, runs `do shell script`, then reopens a new `tell application` block — producing a command line containing both `end tell` and `do shell script` alongside two `tell application` openers. Rationale: Pulled the exact exploitation primitive from the PoC at tabs.go:141: the injected URL contains literal newlines that close one `tell application "Google Chrome"` block with `end tell`, runs `do shell script "id"`, then reopens a second `tell application` block. Detecting the co-occurrence of these three AppleScript tokens on an osascript command line — especially when spawned by anyquery — is a fingerprint of this CVE's exploitation. Cross-checked the GitHub advisory and the affected package paths (julien040/anyquery plugins/chrome, plugins/brave, plugins/edge, plugins/safari). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hrj8-hjv8-mgwc • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/002/
ATT&CKT1059.002 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer testing legitimate multi-application AppleScript automations that nest tell blocks and intentionally use `do shell script` (e.g., DevOps scripts coordinating Chrome + Terminal)
  • Keyboard Maestro / BetterTouchTool / Alfred workflows that build complex AppleScripts on the fly and shell out for unrelated reasons
  • Anyquery legitimate use where the user manually passes a URL containing the literal substring `do shell script` in a benign context (extremely rare)
  • Security tooling / red-team automation that intentionally chains AppleScript and shell commands via `osascript -e`
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Keyboard Maestro Engine", "BetterTouchTool", "Alfred 5", "Hammerspoon") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/Applications/Keyboard Maestro", "/Applications/BetterTouchTool", "/Applications/Alfred"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull full ProcessCommandLine; confirm at least two `tell application` openers separated by an `end tell` + `do shell script` block (the breakout signature). Identify the parent: if it's `anyquery` or a process whose command line references `anyquery`, escalate. Capture the SQL/HTTP traffic that triggered the INSERT/UPDATE on chrome_tabs. 2) Contain — kill the osascript and parent anyquery processes; isolate the host via EDR; disable the anyquery HTTP listener (any local user reaching the endpoint can re-trigger). Snapshot ~/Library/Application Support and Keychain access logs. 3) Hunt — pivot on the user/host: list all child processes of anyquery in the last 30 days; check for `do shell script` patterns invoking curl/wget/python/bash; enumerate anyquery versions across the fleet and confirm patch level >= commit c651df0b8767; audit any HTTP endpoints exposing the anyquery SQL interface beyond localhost.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceInfo_OSPlatform == "macOS" or FolderPath has "/usr/bin/osascript"
| where FileName =~ "osascript"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "do shell script"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "end tell"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "tell application"
| extend TellOpeners = countof(tolower(ProcessCommandLine), "tell application")
| where TellOpeners >= 2
   or InitiatingProcessFileName has "anyquery"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "anyquery"
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "anyquery"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has "osascript"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "do shell script"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "end tell"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "tell application"
| extend TellOpeners = countof(tolower(ActingProcessCommandLine), "tell application")
| where TellOpeners >= 2
   or ParentProcessName has "anyquery"
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has "anyquery"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessId, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AppleScript Code Injection via osascript Breakout Pattern (CVE-2026-47252 / Anyquery)

description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-47252 where anyquery's chrome_tabs plugin interpolates a SQL-controlled URL into an AppleScript template, allowing a payload to close the tell block, inject 'do shell script', and reopen a new tell block.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hrj8-hjv8-mgwc

      - 'end tell'
      - 'tell application'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|contains: 'anyquery'

level: high
@process.executable.path:*/osascript @process.command_line:(*"do shell script"* AND *"end tell"* AND *"tell application"*) AND (@process.parent.executable.path:*anyquery* OR @process.parent.command_line:*anyquery*)

When “Hi, This Is IT” Comes Through Microsoft Teams

Unit 42 (Palo Alto)
2026-06-08 10 use cases 2 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Attackers are increasingly targeting collaboration platforms like Microsoft Teams. Learn the risks and key steps to strengthen your organization's security. The post When “Hi, This Is IT” Comes Through Microsoft Teams appeared first on Unit 42 .

ATT&CKT1190 T1566
Domainsommicrosoft.com
