        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

union

        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)

        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"

        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable cordova-plugin-inappbrowser install on dev endpoint (CVE-2026-47430) AIWeaponization Medium
Hunts for npm / yarn / pnpm / cordova-cli invocations that install cordova-plugin-inappbrowser at a version <6.0.1, the range vulnerable to arbitrary Cordova callback dispatch from InAppBrowser WebView content (CDVWKInAppBrowser.m:560–574). Catches the moment the vulnerable iOS Cordova plugin enters a developer's workspace so the org can patch BEFORE the iOS build ships. Rationale: Article names the exact npm package (`cordova-plugin-inappbrowser`) and the precise vulnerable range (3.1.0 through 6.0.0, fixed 6.0.1). The detection ties the CLI invocations that introduce the package to a version-pin regex covering all vulnerable majors plus the explicit `6.0.0` boundary, and excludes the `6.0.1+` safe pins and non-installing subcommands (uninstall/list). Cross-checked the GHSA URL in the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q42j-x8rq-pjg6
ATT&CKT1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer intentionally pinning to an older version for compatibility testing against legacy cordova-ios
  • Security researcher reproducing CVE-2026-47430 in a sandbox repo
  • CI/CD build agent restoring a legacy package-lock.json that still references 5.x
  • Plugin documentation / `npm view cordova-plugin-inappbrowser` lookups that happen to mention the name
  • Cordova app vendor that has not yet released a 6.0.1-compatible build and pins the last known good version internally
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service") and not (ProcessCommandLine has_any (" uninstall"," remove "," rm "," list "," ls "," view "," info "," search "))
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the affected repo, confirm the install was real (compare the package.json / package-lock.json / config.xml delta against the prior commit, not just the CLI history) and verify the host app actually targets iOS via cordova-ios — Android-only builds aren't exposed by this CVE. 2) Contain: open a PR to bump cordova-plugin-inappbrowser to >=6.0.1, rebuild and re-publish any TestFlight / App Store / enterprise-distribution builds, and where the affected app handles OAuth or session tokens, rotate refresh tokens issued to the prior app version. 3) Hunt: enumerate every repo, CI cache, and developer workspace in the org for cordova-plugin-inappbrowser <6.0.1, push a bulk Dependabot/Renovate update, then for each affected iOS app, check production sign-in / token-issuance logs for the prior 60 days for anomalous Cordova plugin callback patterns (rapid sequential refreshes, mismatched user-agent vs. token issuance).

| order by Timestamp desc

title: Vulnerable cordova-plugin-inappbrowser install (CVE-2026-47430)
id: 8e6c4b8a-3d2a-4e6f-9d7b-1c0e2a4b8d6a
description: |
  Detects npm / yarn / pnpm / cordova / ionic CLI invocations that install
  cordova-plugin-inappbrowser in a version range vulnerable to CVE-2026-47430
  (3.1.0 through 6.0.0). Pinned safe versions (>=6.0.1) are excluded.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q42j-x8rq-pjg6
author: Detection engineering

detection:
  selection_proc:

      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\cordova.cmd'

      - '\ionic.cmd'

level: medium

  - Security researcher reproducing the CVE in a sandbox repo
  - CI agent restoring a legacy package-lock.json that still references 5.x
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\YARN.EXE OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\cordova.cmd OR *\\cordova.exe OR *\\CORDOVA.EXE OR *\\ionic.cmd OR *\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE)) @CommandLine:*cordova-plugin-inappbrowser* (@CommandLine:*install* OR @CommandLine:*add*) -@CommandLine:*cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@6.0.1* -@CommandLine:*cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@6.0.2* -@CommandLine:*cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@6.1* -@CommandLine:*uninstall*

CVE-2026-47430 fleet exposure via Defender TVM (vulnerable cordova-plugin-inappbrowser) AIReconnaissance High
Direct CVE-keyed asset-discovery hunt against Defender Threat & Vulnerability Management for every device the scanner has tagged as carrying CVE-2026-47430. Drives patch prioritisation for iOS Cordova apps whose host plugin (cordova-plugin-inappbrowser) sits below 6.0.1 and is exploitable via attacker-controlled WebView content. Rationale: The advisory ships CVE-2026-47430 against npm:cordova-plugin-inappbrowser <6.0.1. A direct CveId match against the Defender TVM tables is the cleanest, lowest-FP fleet-exposure inventory — it pivots on the article's primary identifier with no need to model the exploit chain itself. The detection has no FP risk from process-level noise because TVM only flags hosts where the scanner actually identified the affected SoftwareVersion. Cross-checked GHSA URL. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q42j-x8rq-pjg6
ATT&CKT1592.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • TVM scan lag — host already patched but inventory not yet rescanned post-bump
  • Developer workstation with two checkout copies of the same repo (counted twice)
  • Build host with the vulnerable plugin cached under a non-active workspace but no longer used
  • Test fixture intentionally pinned to vulnerable version for the project's own CVE regression suite
  • Defender TVM may not natively map every npm-package CVE — coverage gaps yield false negatives rather than false positives, but means an empty result is not conclusive on its own
Response runbook
1) Triage: per device hit, pull the SoftwareName and SoftwareVersion and verify with a manual `npm ls cordova-plugin-inappbrowser` (or grep the affected workspace's package-lock.json) to rule out stale TVM telemetry. 2) Contain: drive each affected developer / build host to upgrade the plugin to >=6.0.1, rebuild any iOS Cordova app that bundled the old version, and pull / revoke any external TestFlight or App Store builds that shipped a vulnerable bundle. 3) Hunt: cross-reference the affected hostnames against MDM and iOS app-inventory to identify which production user-facing apps actually embedded the vulnerable plugin, then in those apps' identity logs (sign-in, OAuth consent, token refresh) look back 60 days for anomalous behaviour consistent with attacker-driven callback spoofing — unexpected camera/contacts/file plugin invocations from app sessions that opened external URLs in InAppBrowser, or token-refresh storms from a single device.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-47430"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            ObservedVersions = make_set(SoftwareVersion),
            Severity = any(VulnerabilitySeverityLevel),
            RecommendedFix = any(RecommendedSecurityUpdate)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName
| order by LastSeen desc

            Severity = any(VulnerabilitySeverityLevel),
            RecommendedFix = any(RecommendedSecurityUpdate)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName
| order by LastSeen desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-47744: Shopper: Authorization bypass and RBAC privilege escalation in team settings

GitHub Security Advisories
2026-06-05 2 use cases 0 techniques 2 kill-chain phases detected

Shopper: Authorization bypass and RBAC privilege escalation in team settings

CVEsCVE-2026-47744

Reconnaissance
Detected

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] HTTP access to Shopper admin team-settings / Livewire endpoints (CVE-2026-47744)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
HTTP access to Shopper admin team-settings / Livewire endpoints (CVE-2026-47744) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts HTTP requests to the vulnerable Shopper admin panel routes — Settings/Team/Index and Settings/Team/RolePermission — including their Livewire AJAX endpoints. Pre-patch (Shopper < 2.8.0) these were reachable by any authenticated panel user and were the only network observable for the authorization-bypass / RBAC privilege-escalation chain disclosed in GHSA-c3qp-2ggw-xjg7. Rationale: The article names exactly two Livewire components — Settings/Team/Index and Settings/Team/RolePermission — as the abuse surface. Livewire routes those component names verbatim through /livewire/update (Livewire v3) and /livewire/message/{component} (v2), so the component string and these endpoints are the highest-fidelity strings available pre-exploit. POST/PUT/PATCH on the role-permission route is the specific action that grants/escalates permissions, distinguishing exploitation from normal page loads. No external IOC corroboration was attempted since the advisory exposes no network IOCs — only source-code paths.
ATT&CKT1190 T1068 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Shopper panel administrators (manage_users holders) creating roles or updating role permissions in normal operations
  • Internal QA / penetration-test exercises against the upgraded (>=2.8.0) panel
  • Application monitoring/uptime probes hitting the admin panel index without authentication (will 302 to login but still appear in HTTP logs)
  • Crawlers / bots probing /livewire/update on any Livewire-built site (broad Livewire scanners)
  • Reverse-proxy retries duplicating the same POST to /livewire/update on transient 5xx
Suppression filter
| where not (User in~ ("admin","superadmin") and ClientIP in ("10.0.0.0/8","192.168.0.0/16")) and not (UserAgent has_any ("Pingdom","UptimeRobot","StatusCake"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the Shopper composer.lock from the affected host and confirm shopper/framework < 2.8.0; if patched, downgrade severity. Identify the authenticated session behind the request (panel session cookie or X-Forwarded-User) and map to the panel user — was it a holder of view_users only? 2) Contain: force-logout all panel sessions, rotate panel admin credentials, and either upgrade to shopper/framework 2.8.0 immediately or block /livewire/update and /admin/settings/team* at the WAF until upgrade. 3) Hunt: dump the roles and role_permission tables and diff against a known-good snapshot — look for newly granted manage_users / edit_orders to non-admin accounts; review the panel users table for unexpected deletions of legitimate administrators; pivot on the source IP across the prior 30 days for any other panel reconnaissance.
// Requires IIS / nginx access logs ingested to a custom table; M365 Defender XDR does not natively capture inbound HTTP to a self-hosted PHP app.
// Pivot via DeviceNetworkEvents for the web server's inbound traffic to the panel's listening port, then triage in the proxy/WAF.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where LocalPort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm.exe","php.exe","nginx.exe","httpd.exe","caddy.exe")
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| summarize Connections = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where Connections > 5
| order by LastSeen desc
let TargetPaths = dynamic(["settings/team","settings.team.index","settings.team.role-permission","settings.team.rolepermission","/livewire/update","/livewire/message/settings.team"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where csUriStem has_any (TargetPaths) or csUriQuery has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Computer, Method=csMethod, Url=strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), Status=scStatus, ClientIP=cIP, UserAgent=csUserAgent, User=csUserName),
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where CsUriStem has_any (TargetPaths) or CsUriQuery has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="AppService", Computer=CsHost, Method=CsMethod, Url=strcat(CsUriStem, iff(isnotempty(CsUriQuery), strcat("?", CsUriQuery), "")), Status=ScStatus, ClientIP=CIp, UserAgent=UserAgent, User=CsUsername),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where RequestURL has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source=DeviceProduct, Computer=DestinationHostName, Method=RequestMethod, Url=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), ClientIP=SourceIP, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, User=SourceUserName)
)
| where Method in~ ("POST","PUT","PATCH") or Url has_any ("role-permission","rolepermission")
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Methods = make_set(Method), Statuses = make_set(Status), UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 5), Users = make_set(User, 10) by ClientIP, Computer, Source
| order by LastSeen desc

description: Detects HTTP requests to Shopper admin panel team-settings routes (Settings/Team/Index, Settings/Team/RolePermission) and their underlying Livewire endpoints, which were the abuse path for CVE-2026-47744 (authorization bypass + RBAC privilege escalation) in shopper/framework versions below 2.8.0.

Unauthenticated POST to AIT-BSC /<name>/start with path-traversal form fields (CVE-2026-47731) AIExploitation High
Hunts the actual exploit shape against the AIT-Core BSC HTTP API: POST to /<name>/start carrying attacker-controlled log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, or path form fields with path-traversal indicators (../, %2e%2e, absolute paths like /etc, /home, /root). Pre-patch AIT-Core <3.1.1 and <2.6.1 lets an unauthenticated remote caller use these fields to redirect log_file writes anywhere ait-bsc can write — corruption of .py modules then yields RCE on next restart. Rationale: Targets the exact REST shape from the article (the Bottle route `/<name>/start` registered in `StreamCaptureManagerServer._route()`) plus the three attacker-influenced form fields named in the bug write-up (log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, path) combined with traversal markers (../ %2e%2e absolute /etc /root /home). The article confirms there is no auth on the route and these fields go straight into `os.path.join` without realpath canonicalisation. Cross-checked against the GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 advisory and the AIT-Core 3.1.1/2.6.1 patch notes which scope the same parameter list. Falcon FDR doesn't natively ship HTTP request bodies so falcon_logscale_query is empty; the same telemetry is covered by NetworkConnectIP4 in UC2. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 • https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Core/releases/tag/3.1.1
ATT&CKT1190 T1565.001
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys, Burp Pro) probing the BSC endpoint as part of a sanctioned scan
  • Mission-ops engineers running `python_poc.py` from the AIT-Core test harness against a lab BSC instance
  • Custom ground-system tooling that legitimately passes log_dir_path to relocate captures between mission phases
  • Health-check probes that POST malformed bodies to /start to verify the route is alive (yields 400 but trips URL pattern)
Suppression filter
and not (SrcIp in ("10.", "172.16.", "192.168.") and UA has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Tenable","Burp","Acunetix","Nmap")) and not (Uri endswith "/healthcheck/start")
Response runbook
Triage: pull the full POST body from the proxy/WAF capture, decode the form fields, and verify whether log_dir_path / path resolves outside the configured `root_log_directory` from bsc.yaml. Pivot on `source IP` to see whether the same caller hit /stats or other handler names. Contain: block the source IP at the perimeter and stop the ait-bsc systemd unit (`systemctl stop ait-bsc`) — do NOT just kill the process because gevent greenlets can keep writing in an infinite-loop bug mentioned in the advisory. Hunt: review DeviceFileEvents for writes by python/ait-bsc into /etc, /root, /home/*/.ssh, site-packages/ait/, or any *.py outside the project tree in the previous 24h; verify SHA256 of any AIT-Core .py against the package wheel hashes; check for outbound TCP from ait-bsc to non-baseline destinations (see related UC2).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionFound","ListeningConnectionCreated")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(python(3(\.\d+)?)?|ait-bsc)(\.exe)?$"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ait-bsc","ait.core.bsc","ait_bsc","StreamCaptureManagerServer","bsc.yaml")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Sessions=count(), AnyLocalPort=any(LocalPort) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let TraversalTokens = dynamic(["log_dir_path","file_name_pattern","..%2F","..%2f","..%5C","..%5c","%2e%2e","path=%2F","path=/etc","path=/root","path=/home","path=/var","path=/tmp","log_dir_path=/"]);
let IISHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)^/[^/]+/start$"
    | where csUriQuery has_any (TraversalTokens) or csUriStem has_any ("%2e%2e", "..")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIp=tostring(cIP), DstPort=tostring(sPort), Uri=csUriStem, Detail=csUriQuery, UA=csUserAgent, Source="W3CIIS";
let CEFHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
    | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)/[^/]+/start(\?|$)"
    | where Message has_any (TraversalTokens) or RequestURL has_any ("%2e%2e", "..")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, DeviceExternalID), SrcIp=SourceIP, DstPort=tostring(DestinationPort), Uri=RequestURL, Detail=Message, UA=RequestClientApplication, Source="CEF";
let SyslogHits = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ProcessName has_any ("ait-bsc","ait_bsc","bsc","python","python3")
    | where SyslogMessage has "/start" and SyslogMessage has_any (TraversalTokens)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIp=HostIP, DstPort="", Uri="/<name>/start", Detail=SyslogMessage, UA="", Source="Syslog";
union IISHits, CEFHits, SyslogHits
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count(), SampleDetail=any(Detail) by Host, SrcIp, Uri, Source
| order by LastSeen desc
title: AIT-Core BSC Unauthenticated Path-Traversal POST (CVE-2026-47731)
id: 8f3b1a2c-9d4e-4f5a-b6c7-d8e9f0a1b2c3
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-47731 — unauthenticated POST to the AIT-Core Binary Stream Capture /<name>/start endpoint carrying path-traversal-indicative form fields (log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, path) or %2e%2e/../ sequences that redirect the log_file write outside the configured root_log_directory.
references:
    - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4
author: Threat Hunter Notebooks
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1190
    - attack.initial_access
    - cve.2026.47731
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection_method:
        cs-method: POST
    selection_uri:
        cs-uri-stem|re: '(?i)^/[^/]+/start$'
    selection_payload:
        cs-uri-query|contains:
            - 'log_dir_path'
            - 'file_name_pattern'
            - '..%2F'
            - '..%2f'
            - '..%5C'
            - '%2e%2e'
            - 'path=%2F'
            - 'path=/etc'
            - 'path=/root'
            - 'path=/home'
            - 'path=/var'
    condition: selection_method and selection_uri and selection_payload
falsepositives:
    - Internal pen-test or vuln-scanner traffic (Tenable, Nessus, Burp Suite Pro)
    - Legitimate ait-bsc admin testing with unusual log_dir_path values
level: high
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:nginx.access OR source:apache.access) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:*/start (@http.url_details.queryString:(*log_dir_path* OR *file_name_pattern* OR *%2e%2e* OR *path%3D%2Fetc* OR *path%3D%2Froot* OR *path%3D%2Fhome*) OR @http.url:(*%2e%2e* OR *..%2F* OR *..%5C*))

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| where match(uri_path, "(?i)^/[^/]+/start$") AND (match(uri_query, "(?i)(log_dir_path|file_name_pattern|path)=") AND (match(uri_query, "(?i)(\.\.|%2e%2e|=%2[Ff]|=/etc/|=/home/|=/root/|=/var/|=/tmp/|=/usr/)") OR match(url, "(?i)(\.\.|%2e%2e)")))
| stats values(urls) as urls values(user_agents) as user_agents min(first_seen) as first_seen max(last_seen) as last_seen sum(count) as hits by src dest uri_path

ait-bsc outbound TCP to public/non-baseline destination (attacker-supplied loc port) AICommand & Control High
Detects ait-bsc / python processes running the ait.core.bsc StreamCaptureManager opening outbound TCP/UDP sessions to non-RFC1918, non-baseline destinations. Per CVE-2026-47731 the unauth /<name>/start endpoint lets a remote caller supply arbitrary `loc` + `port` form values which BSC dutifully `gevent.spawn`s a socket against — making BSC initiate egress to attacker-controlled infrastructure that then streams attacker-chosen bytes back into the file append sink. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article-confirmed primitive: the attacker controls `loc` and `port` in the form body and BSC `gevent.spawn`s a SocketStreamCapturer at that endpoint — i.e. BSC initiates the egress under attacker direction. Process-context match uses the exact module path (`ait.core.bsc`), class name (`StreamCaptureManagerServer`), and config file (`bsc.yaml`) shown in the source excerpt. Sentinel query splits process-context resolution onto ImProcessCreate (which carries ActingProcessCommandLine) and joins by DvcHostname into ImNetworkSession (which does not) — the schema-correct way to express the same logic the Defender query expresses inline. Cross-checked against GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 patch diff which restricts socket creation to validated paths only. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 • https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Core/blob/main/ait/core/bsc.py
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1659
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate ground-station configurations where BSC connects to a public-IP downlink receiver (rare, but check bsc.yaml first)
  • Mission-ops sites running ait-bsc against a cloud-hosted relay (AWS Ground Station, Azure Orbital) which presents as a public IP
  • Engineer testing against a remote development BSC server over a tunnel that egresses to the tunnel endpoint's public IP
  • Updates / pip installs run from the same venv where ait-bsc is installed (mitigated by the process-name filter, but pip can shell into python entrypoints)
Suppression filter
| where not (DstIpAddr in ("<known_ground_station_ip_1>","<known_ground_station_ip_2>")) and not (DstPortNumber in (8080, 8443) and BscCommandLine has "--allow-public-relay")
Response runbook
Triage: pull bsc.yaml from the host and confirm the destination IP+port is NOT in the configured handler list — any unrecognised loc is high-fidelity evil. Capture the BSC handler stats endpoint output (`GET /stats`) to enumerate every currently registered logger and their loc/port/path. Contain: stop the ait-bsc service and revoke any open TCP socket — note the advisory warns of an infinite-loop write bug on close, so plan disk-space monitoring during teardown. Hunt: search DeviceFileEvents for writes by the same ait-bsc PID within the same window, especially to .py / .sh / authorized_keys / cron paths; verify all AIT-Core site-packages files match the wheel hash; pivot the remote IP across DNS / proxy logs to find other internal hosts that reached out to it.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(python(3(\.\d+)?)?|ait-bsc)(\.exe)?$"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ait-bsc","ait.core.bsc","ait_bsc","StreamCaptureManagerServer","bsc.yaml")
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","ConnectionRequest")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Sessions=count(), DistinctRemotes=dcount(RemoteIP) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let BscHosts = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(python(3)?(\.\d+)?|ait-bsc)(\.exe)?$"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ait-bsc","ait.core.bsc","ait_bsc","StreamCaptureManagerServer","bsc.yaml")
    | summarize Cmd=any(ActingProcessCommandLine) by DvcHostname;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where NetworkDirection =~ "Outbound"
| where NetworkProtocol in~ ("TCP","UDP")
| where DvcHostname in ((BscHosts | project DvcHostname))
| where not(ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr))
| where DstIpAddr !startswith "127." and DstIpAddr !startswith "169.254."
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Sessions=count(), Bytes=sum(NetworkBytes) by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol
| join kind=leftouter BscHosts on DvcHostname
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, DvcHostname, BscCommandLine=Cmd, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Sessions, Bytes
| order by FirstSeen desc

Securing CI/CD in an agentic world: Claude Code Github action case

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-06-05 7 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified a prompt injection pathway in Claude Code GitHub Action that allowed access to workflow secrets under specific conditions. This research examines the attack chain, responsible disclosure process, Anthropic's mitigation, and guidance for securing AI-powered CI/CD workflows. The post Securing CI/CD in an agentic world: Claude Code Github action case appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Claude Code Action Read tool exfil: node opens /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux CI runner · [LLM] Claude Code Read tool steered to cloud-credential files on GitHub Actions runner · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GitHub Actions runner: node from Claude Code Action egresses to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub endpoint
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Claude Code Action Read tool exfil: node opens /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux CI runner AIExploitation High
Hunts the exact exploitation primitive Microsoft Threat Intelligence described: the Claude Code Action's in-process Read tool, when steered by an injected prompt, opens /proc/self/environ (or /proc/<pid>/environ) to harvest the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, and OIDC credentials. Pre-fix (claude-code-action <2.1.128) the Bubblewrap sandbox + CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB does not cover Read, so the node process serving Claude Code opens /proc directly — a path almost nothing legitimate touches on a build runner. Rationale: Article names the exact primitive: 'eventually authorized to access /proc/self/environ, reading the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'. We pin on the Linux file path regex + node as the actor. The Read tool runs in-process inside node (not via Bash), so the file event is the only signal — there is no child process to pivot on. Corroborated by Flatt Security (flatt.tech) and Hacker News reporting which describe the same /proc/self/environ exfil chain. Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/claude-code-github-action-flaw-let-one.html • https://oddguan.com/blog/comment-and-control-prompt-injection-credential-theft-claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1212 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Container/process observability agents (datadog-agent, sysdig, falcon-sensor, osquery) using a bundled node helper to enumerate process env for inventory
  • Self-hosted runner image pre-flight scripts that introspect node's own environment for diagnostics (e.g. Node's --inspect tooling)
  • node-based Kubernetes operators (kube-state-metrics ports, Pulumi/CDK preview scripts) iterating /proc to map sibling containers
  • Security tooling that legitimately scans /proc for secret leakage (gitleaks/trufflehog wrapper jobs)
  • Node debugger sessions where a developer manually reads /proc/self/environ to diagnose env-var passing
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("datadog-agent", "sysdig", "falcon-sensor", "osqueryd", "trufflehog", "gitleaks")) and not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/opt/datadog-agent" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/opt/sysdig")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and folder path — confirm node was launched from `_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action*` or `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`. Pull the GitHub run ID from the runner work dir (`/home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>` or env GITHUB_RUN_ID) and fetch the triggering issue/PR body via gh api; look for HTML-comment payloads, /proc references, or Read-tool instructions. Step 2 (contain): Rotate ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN scopes, any OIDC-issued cloud creds, and every other secret exposed to that job. Disable the workflow file until upgraded to claude-code-action ≥2.1.128. For self-hosted runners, isolate the runner host pending forensics. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the same node PID to DeviceNetworkEvents/NetworkConnectIP4 in the surrounding 60s for outbound to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub IPs (exfil destination). Hunt repo-wide for other workflows pinning vulnerable claude-code-action SHAs. Audit recent PRs opened by the AI bot accoun
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"^/proc/(self|\d+)/environ$"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("_work/", "actions-runner", "_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action", "runners/") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessId,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or ActingProcessName =~ "node"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/proc/(self|\d+)/environ$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude-code", "@anthropic-ai", "_actions/anthropics", "actions-runner", "/_work/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId, TargetFilePath, EventType, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Claude Code Read tool steered to cloud-credential files on GitHub Actions runner AIExploitation Medium
Even after the /proc fix in claude-code-action 2.1.128, an attacker who controls the prompt can still steer the Read tool to any path the runner can see. This hunts node — running from the Actions work dir — opening the common secret stores a CI job tends to have on disk: ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc (NPM publish token), ~/.docker/config.json (registry token), ~/.kube/config, ~/.netrc, SSH keys, .env files. Microsoft's article explicitly calls out that 'once an attacker can influence the agent, they might be able to steer it toward sensitive files available inside the CI runner environment'. Rationale: Article: 'once an attacker can influence the agent, they might be able to steer it toward sensitive files available inside the CI runner environment.' We restrict to node spawned from `_work/` or the anthropic action checkout dir so legit user shell activity reading `~/.aws/credentials` doesn't fire. Path list is the GitHub Actions secret canon — npm publish tokens, docker registry creds, GitHub CLI tokens, terraform/pypi publishers — all of which routinely live in runner home dirs. Cross-checked: Flatt's writeup confirms ANTHROPIC_API_KEY + GITHUB_TOKEN + OIDC creds are the named targets, the broader hunt covers what would be next. Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://oddguan.com/blog/comment-and-control-prompt-injection-credential-theft-claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1078.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate `npm publish` step in CI reading ~/.npmrc — node IS the actor, and the file IS a token store
  • AWS CDK / Pulumi / terraform-cdk preview steps where node reads ~/.aws/credentials via the AWS SDK
  • `docker login` wrapper jobs invoking a node-based credential helper that reads ~/.docker/config.json
  • GitHub CLI integration tests that invoke `gh` from node and read ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml
  • Self-hosted runner provisioning script (Ansible/Chef) using node-based tasks to template .env / .npmrc
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm publish", "yarn publish", "docker login", "terraform apply", "terraform plan", "cdk deploy", "cdk synth", "pulumi up", "pulumi preview", "gh auth", "actions/setup-node"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Map the node PID to the GitHub Actions run — InitiatingProcessFolderPath under `_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action*` is the smoking gun. Fetch the triggering issue/PR/comment via `gh api` and look for prompt-injection markers (HTML comments, 'read the file', '/proc/', 'cat ~/.aws'). Validate whether the build step has a legitimate reason to read the file (npm publish, terraform apply). Step 2 (contain): If injection confirmed, rotate every secret the file held (NPM token, AWS keys, kube token, etc.) plus every other secret in the workflow's environment — the agent had broad Read access. Pause the workflow until upgraded past claude-code-action 2.1.128 AND tool-permission scope is reviewed. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep DeviceFileEvents/ImFileEvent for the same node PID reading additional paths in the 5 min before/after; pull DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound from the same PID; query GitHub audit log for any commits/PRs the bot account created in the same window — Microsoft's
let CredPaths = dynamic([".aws/credentials", ".npmrc", ".gitconfig", ".docker/config.json", ".kube/config", ".netrc", "/.env", ".config/gh/hosts.yml", ".terraformrc", ".pypirc"]);

| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths)
   or FolderPath matches regex @"\.ssh/id_(rsa|ed25519|dsa|ecdsa)$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessId,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc

GitHub Actions runner: node from Claude Code Action egresses to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub endpoint AICommand & Control Medium
Closes the loop on the exfiltration step. The Claude Code Action's legitimate outbound destinations are tightly scoped — api.anthropic.com (LLM calls) and the GitHub control plane (api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, ghcr.io, results-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com). When the same node process under `_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action` reaches anything else on a public IP, an attacker is probably steering it to POST the stolen ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OIDC token to their collection endpoint, or to fetch a second-stage payload to plant into a PR (the docs-XSS scenario from Figure 1). Rationale: Article's threat model is clear: 'the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and potentially other credentials available to the runner' get exfiltrated, and the same agent primitive 'create_pull_request_from_changes' lets the attacker reach an external endpoint to receive them or fetch payloads. Allowlist is built from Anthropic's API host plus the GitHub Actions runtime control-plane domains (the only IPs a legit claude-code-action job needs). Anything else from a node process under `_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action` is suspicious by construction. No Sigma — needs cross-table join (process attribution + network destination + DNS). Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://www.securityweek.com/claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot-agents-vulnerable-to-prompt-injection-via-comments/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Workflow that legitimately uses Claude Code Action to call a 3rd-party API as part of the task (e.g. Jira/Linear integration via MCP)
  • Runner using a corporate egress proxy that rewrites destination hostnames (proxy IP shows instead of api.anthropic.com)
  • GitHub-hosted runner with dynamic Azure egress IPs not yet enriched to githubusercontent.com hostname
  • Telemetry shippers (datadog-agent, splunk forwarder) running on self-hosted runner reaching their own SaaS endpoints
  • Package install steps that reach registry.npmjs.org / pypi.org for transitive deps pulled by claude-code-action setup
Suppression filter
| where not(RemoteUrl has_any ("datadoghq.com", "splunkcloud.com", "sentry.io", "registry.npmjs.org", "pypi.org", "files.pythonhosted.org", "registry.yarnpkg.com"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Resolve the destination — WHOIS / passive DNS / VT for the IP and any DNS name. Pull the GitHub run ID via the runner work dir, then `gh api` the triggering event body for prompt-injection markers (HTML comments, 'POST to', 'curl', URL strings matching the destination). Compare against your runner egress allowlist. Step 2 (contain): Block the destination IP/domain at egress; rotate ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN scopes, and any OIDC-issued cloud creds the workflow held; disable the workflow file. For self-hosted runners, snapshot disk + memory before reimaging. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to the file-event UCs above on the same node PID to see what got read; query GitHub audit log for branches/PRs/commits the AI bot account opened in the same window (the article's Figure 1 attack used the same agent to commit XSS into docs); search the org for other repos pinning vulnerable claude-code-action SHAs.
let RunnerNode = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "node"
    | where FolderPath has_any ("_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action", "_work/", "actions-runner")
         or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action")
    | project NodeTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, NodePid = ProcessId, NodeCmd = ProcessCommandLine, NodeFolder = FolderPath;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where not(RemoteUrl has_any ("anthropic.com", "api.github.com", "githubusercontent.com", "githubapp.com", "githubassets.com", "ghcr.io", "actions.githubusercontent.com"))
| where isnotempty(RemoteIP)
| join kind=inner RunnerNode on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.NodePid
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, NodeCmd, NodeFolder, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| summarize HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), Destinations = make_set(RemoteUrl, 20), DestIPs = make_set(RemoteIP, 20)
           by DeviceName, NodeFolder, RemotePort
| order by FirstSeen desc
let AllowList = dynamic(["anthropic.com", "api.github.com", "githubusercontent.com", "githubapp.com", "githubassets.com", "ghcr.io", "actions.githubusercontent.com"]);
let RunnerHosts = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or TargetProcessName endswith "/node"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action", "@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action", "/_work/")
    | distinct DvcHostname;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname in (RunnerHosts)
| where isnotempty(DstHostname)
| where DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." 
     and not(DstIpAddr matches regex @"^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.") 
     and DstIpAddr !startswith "127." and DstIpAddr !startswith "169.254."
| where not(DstHostname has_any (AllowList))
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), HitCount = count(), SampleUrl = any(Url)
           by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol
| order by FirstSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 OR source:linux.auditd) (@process.name:node OR @process.executable.path:*/node) (@ParentImage:*claude-code* OR @process.command_line:*claude-code* OR @process.command_line:*@anthropic-ai*) NOT (@DestinationHostname:*.anthropic.com OR @DestinationHostname:*.github.com OR @DestinationHostname:*.githubusercontent.com OR @DestinationHostname:*.ghcr.io OR @DestinationHostname:*.githubapp.com OR @DestinationHostname:*.githubassets.com) NOT CIDR(@network.destination.ip, 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12, 127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/\/node$/i
| regex("(actions-runner|_work|_actions\\/anthropics\\/claude-code-action)", field=ContextImageFileName, strict=false)
| RemoteAddressIP4!=/^(10\.|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.|127\.|169\.254\.)/
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest | DomainName!=/(anthropic\.com|github\.com|githubusercontent\.com|ghcr\.io|githubapp\.com|githubassets\.com)$/i | groupBy([aid, FirstIP4Record], function=collect(DomainName, as=resolved_domain))}, field=[aid, RemoteAddressIP4=FirstIP4Record])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort, resolved_domain], function=count(as=conns))
| conns > 0

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port values(All_Traffic.dest_ip) as dest_ip from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app="node" AND All_Traffic.src_category="github_actions_runner" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="private" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.process_id | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where NOT match(dest, "(?i)(\.anthropic\.com|api\.github\.com|githubusercontent\.com|githubapp\.com|githubassets\.com|ghcr\.io|actions\.githubusercontent\.com)$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

DbGate loadReader functionName code injection (CVE-2026-47670) AIExploitation High
Hunts HTTP POST requests to the DbGate /runners/load-reader endpoint carrying an injection-shaped functionName (newline + import('child_process') + execSync). Article-specific to the unsanitized template interpolation in packages/api/src/controllers/runners.js. Rationale: Targets the article-specific URI path /runners/load-reader together with the bypass primitives the writeup names verbatim (child_process import, execSync, require=null bypass). The newline (%0A) is the structural injection marker the PoC requires to break out of the template literal.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red-team or vulnerability scanner explicitly testing CVE-2026-47670
  • DbGate developer integration tests that include the literal endpoint and a benign functionName (allowlist by source IP)
  • Legitimate WAF / DAST tooling (Burp, ZAP, Nuclei) probing the host
  • Backups/exports tooling that proxies through DbGate but never sends child_process strings
Suppression filter
and not SourceIP in ("<scanner-cidr>", "<redteam-ip>") and not csUserName in~ ("dbgate-ci", "dast-bot")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request body for the matching session, decode any URL-encoded newlines, and confirm functionName contains a newline plus child_process/import/execSync. Identify the authenticated DbGate user from the JWT and the source IP. 2) Contain: revoke the DbGate user's credentials, rotate any DB connection passwords referenced in DbGate config, block the source IP at the proxy, and snapshot the DbGate container for forensics before restart. 3) Hunt: from the same source IP and same authenticated user, pivot to UC2 (node spawning shell), egress connections from the DbGate container, and any FileWritten events under /tmp/_rce_* or other UUID-suffixed paths that match the PoC's jslout pattern.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "/runners/load-reader" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "/runners/load-reader"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectMarkers = dynamic(["child_process","execSync","await import","%0A","\\nvar ","\\nawait"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod == "POST" and csUriStem endswith "/runners/load-reader"
  | extend Payload = strcat(csUriQuery, " ", csUserAgent)
  | where Payload has_any (SuspectMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "POST" and RequestURL has "/runners/load-reader"
  | where RequestURL has_any (SuspectMarkers) or Message has_any (SuspectMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, Message),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpMethod =~ "POST" and Url has "/runners/load-reader"
  | where Url has_any (SuspectMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpStatusCode)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DbGate node process spawning shell child (post-exploit RCE) AIInstallation High
Hunts for the dbgate / node.js process spawning a shell or command interpreter, which is the post-exploitation footprint of CVE-2026-47670's child_process.execSync call. The legitimate DbGate runtime does not spawn /bin/sh or cmd.exe as children, so any such child is suspicious in container or host context. Rationale: DbGate's normal runtime never spawns a POSIX shell or Windows command interpreter — the article explicitly states the bypass is `(await import('child_process')).execSync(...)`, so child-process creation under a node parent named dbgate is the direct execution-time signal. Pairs with UC1 to give one network-side and one host-side detection of the same chain.
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DbGate plugin or admin shell-out feature in a customized fork (verify against vendor binary)
  • DbGate container's entrypoint script invoking sh at startup (filter on container start time)
  • Backup / cron sidecars that exec sh inside the dbgate container's PID namespace
  • Developer attaching to the dbgate pod via kubectl exec (filter by InitiatingProcessCommandLine containing 'docker-exec' or by interactive TTY)
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("docker-entrypoint.sh","yarn start","npm start") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c","node "))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full child cmdline and walk back to the parent node process. If the cmdline matches recon (id, whoami, uname -a) or contains base64/curl/wget, treat as confirmed RCE. Correlate with UC1 within the same 60s window from the same DbGate instance. 2) Contain: kill the dbgate container/pod, isolate the host, rotate the DbGate admin password and any DB credentials in DbGate's connection store (LOGIN_PASSWORD_*, PASSWORD_con*). 3) Hunt: pivot on the dbgate host's outbound network connections in the prior hour, look for /tmp/_rce_*.jsonl style file writes referenced in the PoC, search for newly created users / SSH keys, and check the DB engines DbGate had connections to for follow-on activity from the dbgate host's IP.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","dbgate","dbgate.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/app/packages/api", "/dbgate", "dbgate")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ash","busybox","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/|\\)(node|dbgate)(\.exe)?$" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "dbgate"
  | where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/|\\)(sh|bash|dash|zsh|ash|busybox|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh(\.exe)?)$"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","dbgate.exe") 
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ProcessName in~ ("auditd","audit")
  | where SyslogMessage has "type=EXECVE" and SyslogMessage has_any ("/bin/sh","/bin/bash","/bin/dash")
  | where SyslogMessage has_any ("node","dbgate")
  | project TimeGenerated, HostName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
